Graphics: virtual desktop mode and DPI settings

Changing only ProductName changes a registry string; it is not equivalent to the winecfg version setting, NT version reporting, or API support. Prefer winecfg for setting the emulated version, or a winetricks version verb supported by the current runner. Registry keys may be historical WineD3D options that DXVK/VKD3D or your chosen runner does not read. Before editing, export the relevant keys or keep a prefix backup, and record the old values. A successful reg add does not prove that a graphics setting has taken effect.

Mods such as ReShade may place a same-named DLL in the game directory. Whether it loads first depends on DLL search behavior, the runner version, overrides, process bitness, and how the game is launched. The automatic Wine 11.6 rules claimed by the source material alone cannot guarantee that it works.

Use WINEDEBUG=+loaddll or the selected runner's logs to confirm the actual load location. First verify the mod's source and game support, keep the original files, and undo individual overrides if problems arise. Disabling NVAPI may also affect features such as DLSS/Reflex; incorrect graphics-DLL overrides can prevent startup. Do not treat a local DLL as a trusted or universal performance patch.

HDR depends on the entire display chain. Check all of the following: HDR support in the game, the DXVK/VKD3D or native rendering path, the runner/WSI, the compositor or Gamescope, the GPU driver, the display connection, and the HDR monitor. A compatible monitor or a single environment variable is not enough to prove correct output.

Confirm the compositor's HDR state, the game's settings, and the output path separately, then examine brightness, color, and screenshot/display behavior. A single table of minimum kernel, Plasma, driver, or Proton versions cannot guarantee that every display chain works.
Native Wayland operation (as distinct from XWayland)

Setting a variable does not prove that winewayland.drv is in use. Confirm the driver in the logs, then test the application's requirements for windows, scaling, mouse input, input methods, the clipboard, fullscreen, and VR. XWayland may be more compatible in some cases; native Wayland cannot be guaranteed to have lower latency or to work better when combined with Gamescope.

GPU selection operates at several layers: Mesa device selection, NVIDIA PRIME render offload, Vulkan ICD/physical-device enumeration, and adapter selection within DXVK/VKD3D itself. Do not treat DRI_PRIME=1 as a universal switch for every hybrid-GPU setup.

The Vulkan ICD path operates at the library-loading layer; specifying it does not select a particular physical GPU. In a sandbox especially, do not hard-code host JSON paths. If the selected VKD3D-Proton supports VKD3D_VULKAN_DEVICE, verify the index against the devices actually enumerated in that environment. Do not assume that 1 always means the discrete GPU.

Verify the device using the target game's DXVK/VKD3D logs, HUD, and actual load, and record differences between Flatpak/Steam runtime diagnostics and host diagnostics. Looking only at the first vulkaninfo entry or one environment variable is not sufficient validation.

Frame generation requires integration in the game itself, a supported GPU and driver, the correct components, and appropriate game settings. Ordinary DLSS Super Resolution, Frame Generation, and Multi Frame Generation are distinct capabilities. Downloading a newer DLL does not add them to arbitrary games or graphics cards.

Next, check whether the game offers the corresponding options and whether its runtime logs show the intended DLL loading. Measure the actual displayed frame rate, base rendered frame rate, and latency. The GE README supported an optional download mechanism when checked, but one fixed minimum DLL version cannot describe multi-frame-generation support across all releases.
Memory, file handles, and configuration tuning

Measure and identify the bottleneck first, then change one parameter at a time. File-descriptor limits may affect older synchronization paths that use many handles, but an ulimit of hundreds of thousands should not be applied indiscriminately to all current Proton versions.

The commands above read diagnostic values. If a process's soft limit genuinely needs adjustment, keep it within the hard limit and base the change on logs. vm.max_map_count and the handle limit govern different resources. THP can affect specific workloads, but it should not be disabled by default, nor should a tutorial use sudo to write to /sys and change system-wide policy. Persistent NixOS settings belong in declarative modules, with build, activation, and runtime results validated separately.

A configuration file's presence in a directory does not prove that it was read. Check the effective settings in the logs, then compare frame times, stability, and resource use in the same scenario. Remove the switches and configuration file to restore the baseline; more parameters should not be mistaken for better performance.

Version note: the variables above belong to Wine, official Proton, GE, DXVK, VKD3D, and historical patches. Unknown or obsolete variables may be silently ignored.
